/* Wave 9v — the name is read on the pro.selector: /* Wave 9v — the name is read on the profile's own surface, never across the photo. Wave 6t pulled the identity row up over the cover so the portrait overlaps the band, and the words travelled with it: the name, the lock and the presence line landed on the picture, where a bright cover made them faint. The row still overlaps — the portrait keeps the cover's bottom edge — and everything that is words starts under it, on the dark surface the profile is read on. One variable carries the overlap, so the band, the portrait and the words can never disagree about it. */ .nexusOwnerProfile

/* Wave 10 — the name reads on one line,.selector: /* Wave 10 — the name reads on one line, the portrait fills its own row, and the pencil opens a page instead of turning the hero into a form. The band above the identity is either the cover photo or the shelf of saved stories, and the moving band of facts stays with the owner on a profile that is not public. One variable carries the portrait's size and one carries where the words start under the cover, so the band, the portrait and the words can never disagree about the row they share. */ .nexusOwnerProfile

/* Wave 10 — the name reads on one line, the portrait fills its own row, and the pencil opens a page instead of turning the hero into a form. The band above the identity is either the cover photo or the shelf of saved stories, and the moving band of facts stays with the owner on a profile that is not public. One variable carries the portrait's size and one carries where the words start under the cover, so the band, the portrait and the words can never disagree about the row they share. */ .nexusOwnerProfile

/* Without a cover there is nothing to o.selector: /* Without a cover there is nothing to overlap and nothing for the words to clear, and a profile that never had a cover must not pay for a band it does not show. */ .nexusOwnerProfile[data-profile-cover="0"]

/* The other half of the same choice: a.selector: /* The other half of the same choice: a profile that shows the shelf of saved stories instead of a cover. The rail is in the markup either way and the section says which of the two is on screen, so switching is one attribute; with no cover over it there is nothing to overlap, which is what --heroOverlap:0 says to every rule that reads it. It sits on its own row now: the name line, then the shelf, then the band. */ .nexusOwnerProfile[data-cover-mode="stories"]
